headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: a month-long slide has pushed price under its 200-day line

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: The model's long-run posture is still to grow acquisition, but this is a week to hold the planned level, not push. A Rally watch drop window is open, Bitcoin is down about 9% in a week and 16% in a month, it now sits about 6% under its 200-day average and right on its 200-week average, and the mood is in extreme fear. Keep acquisition running at a steady pace with trust and education angles, hold trader-focused promotions and keep a reserve; speed up only if price wins back $73,044 (the 200-day average) and, for a bigger push, $80,571 (the 50-day average).

reasons: The 200-day average ($73,044) is still rising, about 5% over 90 days.
Up about 9% over 90 days, but down about 16% over the last 30.
BTC ($68,799) is about 6% under its 200-day average, 1% above the 200-week.
Fear & Greed at 20 (extreme fear); 23 days under the 50-day average ($80,571).
watch: Bitcoin is sitting almost exactly on its 200-week average ($68,118), the last big floor, while many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money. A close back above $70,750 would steady the week, while a close below $68,118 would turn it clearly down and put $62,819 (the 90-day low) in view.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run picture still leans up, but the week is soft and Bitcoin is now testing its last big floor. At about $68,799 it has closed under its 50-day average for 23 days, sits about 15% below it and about 18% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 20 (extreme fear); PANews reports about $1.23 billion of bets on a rise were forced to close in 24 hours as price fell below $69,000. A normal week swings about $4,069, so a close above $70,750 (top of a typical week's swing) would steady things, a close below $68,118 (the 200-week average) would turn the week clearly down, and in between it stays choppy. Safety and explainer messaging fits better than any promotion this week.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still show price about 9% higher and about 94% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 16% and a lot of people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which makes dips sharper. Price is well under its 50-day average, so it must win back $80,571 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb; until then, keep bigger campaign pushes for after the 8 December Fed meeting.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but more weakly, because the 200-day average itself is still rising (about 5% over 90 days) while price is now about 6% under it. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $73,044 (the 200-day average) again; $68,118 (the 200-week average) is the floor being tested right now, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A run of closes below the 200-week average would weaken this picture clearly and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
